statement: Make possession, cultivation and use of cannabis free from prosecution

summary.why: The ALCP says cannabis prohibition is unworkable and discriminatory, wastes public money and fuels the black market.
summary.how: Part of the party's 'Policy Minimum Programme': no prosecution for possessing, growing or using cannabis and cannabis/hemp products.

statement: Create regulated R18 cannabis commerce like alcohol and tobacco, but with no promotion

summary.why: The ALCP says cannabis prohibition is unworkable and discriminatory, wastes public money and fuels the black market.
summary.how: Legal adult-only sales with no advertising or promotional aspects, with details fine-tuned by a policy council.

statement: Provide for medicinal cannabis, including home-grown medicine and prescribed preparations

summary.why: The party says legal access would promote safer modes of use such as vaporisation and mouth sprays.
summary.how: Establish therapeutic applications of cannabis, allowing both home-grown medicinal cannabis and prescribed preparations.

statement: Enable full-scale hemp production, prioritising local low-cost biofuel, fibre and hurd

summary.why: The party says hemp would create jobs (especially in depressed regions), cut emissions and pollution, save forests and improve soils.
summary.how: Allow full-scale cannabis-hemp farming and use, with priority for localised biofuel production and fibre and hurd for building materials, paper, plastics and textiles; hemp seed as food.

statement: Expunge all cannabis convictions and apologise for prohibition

summary.why: The party says up to 20,000 people a year are convicted of cannabis offences and that Māori are four to five times more likely to be convicted.
summary.how: Wipe all cannabis convictions; the 2020 addendum adds that apologies must be made for the injustices of prohibition.

statement: Hold a prohibition 'truth and reconciliation' commission

summary.why: The party says Parliament has a duty to challenge injustice and break down prejudice.
summary.how: A full commission on prohibition 'in the interests of accountability'.

statement: Set up a tobacco, alcohol and cannabis authority (Drugs Policy Council) to regulate recreational substances

summary.why: The party says credible, harm-reduction drug education is impossible under current 'double standards'.
summary.how: A single regulator to develop the regulatory framework for recreational substances, with 'adults only' enforcement and honest drug education in schools funded from prohibition savings.

statement: Redirect prohibition enforcement money to health, education, community and serious crime

summary.why: The party says police would be freed up for 'real crime' and public trust in the law would improve.
summary.how: Shift funds currently spent enforcing cannabis laws into health, education, community and employment, and more police and court resources for serious crime.

statement: Stop overseas cannabis offences being a barrier to immigrating to New Zealand

summary.why: The party says it has no other immigration position beyond inclusiveness and tolerance.
summary.how: Cannabis offences in other jurisdictions should not bar migrants.

statement: Reallocate drug-war resources to border security and civil defence

summary.why: The party says the international war on drugs aids organised crime and terrorism.
summary.how: Resources freed by ending the cannabis 'drug war' would strengthen border security and civil defence.

statement: Allow at least five cannabis plants per household and affordable micro-licences for small growers

summary.why: Part of the party's 2020 'cottage industry' ideas, which it says are still under discussion.
summary.how: A 'bare minimum' five-plant home-grow allowance, affordable micro-licences for existing growers, Kiwi seed strains, safe edibles, quality-controlled retail products and protection against racially loaded enforcement; an age limit more consistent with alcohol and tobacco.
